paragraphs.text: On 22 January 1879, eleven days after the British invaded the Zulu Kingdom, a Zulu force of some 20,000 warriors attacked a portion of the British main column at Isandlwana.
During the final hours of the British defeat there, a large contingent of Zulu warriors broke off and travelled ten kilometres to attack the mission station at Rorke's Drift.
A vastly outnumbered British force under Lieutenants John Chard and Gonville Bromhead held it, and the battle holds the record for the most Victoria Crosses awarded for a single battle.
Hattingspruit, a coal mining town, was established here in the 1880s.

The Battle of Talana Hill, in 1899, was the first major clash of the Second Boer War, and the Battle of Elandslaagte, fought while the Boers were invading Natal, was one of the few decisive British victories.
On 30 October 1899 a British sortie from Ladysmith ended in disaster, and the Boers began a siege of the town on 2 November 1899.
Redvers Buller's attempts to relieve it started on 15 December 1899 at the Second Battle of Colenso, where the Boers repelled British forces on the Tugela River.
The Battle of Vaal Krantz, in 1900, was his third failed attempt to fight past Louis Botha's Boer army.
From 14 February to 27 February 1900, at the Battle of the Tugela Heights, Buller's army forced Botha's army to lift the siege, which lasted until 28 February 1900.
